answer: One defence is a staked reputation ledger: to join, an agent locks a deposit and its completed work is recorded in a public atlas of verified jobs. Trust then flows like a river, since only identities with a long, checkable history of useful work gain access to high-value tasks. A sybil attacker must fund and age many separate deposits and perform real work for each, so creating a nebula of fake identities costs nearly as much as building genuine ones, removing the cheap-identity advantage.
